title: Every nation (Revelation 7:9–17)
hookLine: a great multitude of every nation and tongue, and God wipes away every tear

cards: John hears a number first: "An hundred and forty and four thousand," sealed from the tribes of Israel, twelve thousand from each tribe, named one by one. A careful count.
Then he looks, and what he sees can't be counted at all. Two days ago he heard lion and saw lamb, and some readers notice the same move here: a number heard, a crowd seen, too big for numbers.
People from everywhere, standing before the throne in white, holding palm branches, all shouting at once.

teach.b: First, the crowd, in the King James words: "a great multitude, which no man could number, of all nations, and kindreds, and people, and tongues, stood before the throne, and before the Lamb, clothed with white robes, and palms in their hands."
Notice the list. The text doesn't melt them into one. In heaven, by this picture, languages are still languages.

And they cry together: "Salvation to our God which sitteth upon the throne, and unto the Lamb." Second, who they are. An elder asks John: "What are these which are arrayed in white robes? and whence came they?"
And John, who has seen so much already, says: "Sir, thou knowest." You tell me.
The elder answers: "These are they which came out of great tribulation, and have washed their robes, and made them white in the blood of the Lamb."
Robes made white by washing them in blood: Christians read it as the Lamb's death making people clean. Third, the care.

teach.h: NO MORE HUNGER, NO MORE THIRST.
teach.b: After yesterday's famine: "They shall hunger no more, neither thirst any more; neither shall the sun light on them, nor any heat."
The Lamb, the one who was slain, becomes their shepherd, and "shall lead them unto living fountains of waters."

teach.h: GOD SHALL WIPE AWAY ALL TEARS.
teach.b: Fourth, the tears: "and God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes." It echoes Isaiah: "the Lord GOD will wipe away tears from off all faces." Wiping tears takes nearness; you have to be close enough to touch a face.
Yesterday the question was how long. Today the answer isn't a date. It's a hand.

how: Revelation 7:9–17 is read at some Christian funerals and on All Saints' Day, as a picture of the saints from every nation gathered before God.

games.q: you're John. an elder points at the crowd in white and asks: who are these, and where did they come from? what do you say?
o: give a full list of names.
games.why: John admits he doesn't know, and the elder tells him: "these are they which came out of great tribulation."

practice: Let faces come, slowly, from everywhere you can think of, different skin, clothes and languages, nobody asked to stop being who they are: a neighbor, a coworker, someone you've argued with, people you'll never meet.
If you pray, join the crowd's own words, "Salvation to our God which sitteth upon the throne, and unto the Lamb"; if not, just stand among them for a while, and breathe.

wordCard.voice: Every nation. John's great multitude that no one could number, from all nations, kindreds, peoples and tongues, fed and led by the Lamb, every tear wiped away.

orig.note: Greek: a nation, a people. the word behind 'nations' in Revelation 7:9.

carryVoice: Your line: every tear wiped. Not from across a room, but close enough to touch a face. Thirteen hundred days now.
